newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sugar beet harvest almost complete.
newsitem.headline: French sugar beet harvest almost complete.

text.p: The sugar beet harvest is virtually complete in France, with 95 percent of the crop lifted from the ground and 78 percent delivered to refineries, data collected by the CGB beet planters' federation up to November 19 showed.
At the same date last year 97 percent of the crop had been harvested and 74 percent delivered to refineries.
The survey, which is due for official release later this week, indicated sugar content at delivery was 18.9 percent compared with 18.8 percent on November 6 and 17.5 percent on November 19, 1995.
The latest data on beet yields was not immediately available but data up to November 10 showed yields of 53.7 tonnes per hectare, down from 58.2 tonnes at the same time last year.
Data collected by planters suggested a final beet yield of 55 tonnes per hectare, down from 59 tonnes last year.
Growers said they expected refineries to complete beet processing operations some three days ahead of last year.
Refineries had fewer beets to process this year, while the high sugar content made processing operations easier.
Last year on average refineries stopped processing beets around December 12.
The beet area fell to an estimated 422,000 hectares from 425,000 hectares last year.
